facts.label: Present perfect com already e just
facts.sub: Use have/has + particípio. Already (já) e just (acabou de) ficam entre have/has e o particípio: The train has already left. It has just arrived.

facts.label: Já saiu
facts.sub: Use has already + particípio para dizer que algo aconteceu: The train has already left. Already fica antes do particípio e mostra que ficou tarde para agir.

facts.label: Acabou de chegar
facts.sub: Use has just + particípio para algo muito recente: The next train has just arrived. I have just sent a message. Mostra que foi há poucos minutos.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Already means something happened earlier than expected.
Just means a long time ago.
items.why: Just means a very short time ago.

items.s: We say “The train has just arrive.”

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Already means something happened earlier than expected. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
Just means a long time ago. → Falso (Just means a very short time ago.)
We say “The train has just arrive.” → Falso (We say arrived.)

pages.title: A rainy London station · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a rainy Monday morning at a busy station in London. A voice makes an announcement about a delay. People stand on the platform and check their phones. Ela waits by the board with a coffee. Her friend Theo runs in with a heavy bag. He looks at the empty track and sighs.

“Theo, we’re late! The eight fifteen train has already left.” says Ela. “Oh no. Has the next one arrived yet?” says Theo. “Not yet. The board says nine ten. It has already been late twice this week.” says Ela.
